pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:31 The fairness and discrimination gates exit 0 under --strict when a cohort is empty, for example a --count below the 6 behaviours. A run that measured no fairness at all is therefore certified the same way as a passing run. The standard says absence in the gate's own sample must be REFUSE, spelled as failure when the protocol has only two states.

techniques.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:31 not_evaluable comes from an empty cohort in the harness's own sample (the gate's vision, not the subject's world), yet it exits 0 under --strict. The report states the skip loudly, but the exit code certifies. calibrate.evaluate_gate gets this right (line 280: a judged-but-unmeasured dimension fails), so the two gates in one module resolve the same case in opposite ways.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/calibrate.py:446 The exit-code path traces directly from the GATE failure reasons to `return 1` under --strict. Without --strict the command is a report and is labelled as one.
pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_devcase_calibrate.py:198 The acceptance gate is proven red by a seeded low case-mean, beside a passing control.

pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:647 Identifies a layer that makes reliability unfailable: deterministic templates always pass _check. A separate error_fallbacks condition makes --strict able to refuse that run.
pipeline/jobfit/devcase/submission_eval.py:664 The self-grading refusal names a concrete remedy the operator can apply through use-case routing.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline-tenancy.test.ts:7 The per-statement tenancy guard for pipeline_entries walks a hand-written list of 5 files (line 17). A grep finds about 29 non-test files that query pipeline_entries, including pipeline-calibration.ts in this same context, and none of the others are judged. tenancy-coverage.test.ts explicitly delegates per-statement scoping to per-table guards like this one, and the header's 'EVERY file' claim is false.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline-tenancy.test.ts:7 The gate's population is enumerated by hand rather than derived from a tree walk, so a new file that queries pipeline_entries is never judged and nothing says so. The >=30 floor cannot see a file it never reads.
app/_lib/db/pipeline-tenancy.test.ts:67 Checks the instrument before the result: a collapsed SQL extraction fails instead of passing with zero queries.
app/_lib/db/pipeline-tenancy.test.ts:58 Pins the predicate's teeth with a deliberately wrong fixture, so the scoping rule is shown able to refuse.
app/_lib/db/pipeline-close-guard.test.ts:142 Runs the shipped SQL itself against a real SQLite database instead of matching a retyped copy, and keeps an unguarded control as the non-vacuity case.
app/_lib/db/pipeline-close-guard.test.ts:54 Renaming the function the detector keys on makes the guard fail loudly instead of silently dropping the finding.
